dash.offline.title: Cannot connect to the node

dash.stall.title: The sync may have stopped
dash.stall.fewUtreexo: Only {n} Utreexo-capable peer(s) are connected. Floresta needs at least {min} to make progress.
dash.stall.noProgress: The validated height has not changed for over 10 minutes.
dash.uptime.tip: How long florestad has been running (uptime)
dash.latest.tip: Best block hash (bestblockhash) and its time
dash.stage.caption: {n} Utreexo trees (roots)
peers.lead: Your party is the peers florestad is connected to. Utreexo-capable peers send the proofs Floresta needs, so it needs at least two of them.
peers.summary.note: Utreexo peers are highlighted in green below.
peers.warn.title: Not enough Utreexo friends
peers.invite.label: Peer address (ip:port)
peers.invite.hint: Runs addnode <ip:port> add. IPv4, [IPv6]:port or a bare IP.
peers.invite.invalid: Enter an IP address, optionally with a port, like 203.0.113.7:8333 or [2001:db8::1]:8333.
peers.invite.confirmBody: florestad will add the peer to its list and try to connect now.
peers.invite.sent: Invitation sent to {addr}. It appears below once the handshake starts.
peers.disconnect.title: Disconnect this peer?
peers.disconnect.body: florestad will drop the connection to {addr}. It may connect to other peers instead.
block.lead: A simple block explorer. Headers are stored locally and show up instantly; Floresta does not keep block bodies, so they are fetched from peers on demand.
block.search.label: Height or block hash
block.search.invalid: Enter a block height (a number) or a 64-character block hash.
block.fetching.note: Floresta does not store blocks, so getblock asks the network. This can take up to 30 seconds.
block.fetchFailed: Could not fetch the block body
block.fetchFailed.body: The peers did not deliver it in time. The header above is still valid.
block.txids.note: Floresta only looks up transactions that belong to your watch-only wallet, so the IDs are listed without links.
wallet.lead: Floresta's wallet is watch-only: it follows your addresses using public keys (xpubs inside descriptors). It never needs, and must never see, a private key.
wallet.empty: No descriptors yet. Add one below.
wallet.watchOnly.title: Watch-only
wallet.watchOnly.body: Paste only an xpub or a descriptor with public keys. Anything containing a private key (xprv, tprv, WIF) is blocked before it is sent.
wallet.add.label: Descriptor (or a bare xpub / tpub)
wallet.add.hint: Runs loaddescriptor. A bare xpub/tpub is added as wpkh(KEY/0/*) and wpkh(KEY/1/*) (receive and change).
wallet.add.confirmBody: florestad will start watching the addresses of this descriptor.
wallet.add.confirmBare: This bare key will be added as two descriptors (receive and change).
wallet.add.done: Descriptor added. Rescan if it has older transactions.
wallet.err.private: That looks like a private key. It was removed from the form and nothing was sent. Floresta only needs public keys (xpub / tpub).
wallet.err.shape: This does not look like a descriptor. Example: wpkh(tpubD…/0/*)
wallet.err.ibd: Floresta is still syncing. Try again once it is up to date.
wallet.err.invalid: florestad says the descriptor is invalid. Check the key and the checksum.
wallet.rescan.hint: Runs rescanblockchain. Floresta checks BIP 158 block filters and only downloads the blocks that may concern your wallet. With a date, a higher confidence looks further back.
wallet.rescan.err.height: Heights must be whole numbers of 0 or more.
wallet.rescan.err.order: The start must be before the stop.
wallet.rescan.err.beyond: The start is beyond the current height ({tip}).
wallet.rescan.started: Rescan started. florestad logs the blocks it finds for your wallet.
forest.lead: Floresta does not keep the UTXO set (every unspent coin). It keeps a Utreexo accumulator instead: a small forest of Merkle trees, of which it only remembers the roots. Peers send proofs along with each block.
forest.compare.lead: That is all: {size} of tree tops.
forest.compare.body: A regular full node keeps the whole UTXO set, several gigabytes (about 10 GB on mainnet). That is roughly {ratio}× more than this forest.
forest.scaleNote: Trees are not to scale: getroots returns the root hashes but not the number of leaves, so only the number of trees is real.
forest.explain.1: Each tree is a Merkle tree whose leaves are coins. When a coin is spent, its proof shows the path up to a root, so I can check it without the whole list!
forest.explain.2: The number of trees follows the binary digits of the number of coins, which is why it goes up and down as blocks arrive.
